thread.title_full: Jenkins' tenure at Daniel Boone ends as Tennessee High passes for five scores

author: BRIAN WOODSON\nbwoodson@sixriversmedia.com
title: Jenkins' tenure at Daniel Boone ends as Tennessee High passes for five scores
text: BRISTOL, Tenn. — After 24 years as head coach at Daniel Boone, Jeremy Jenkins will pass the whistle to someone else. Tennessee High did its own kind of passing on Thursday night, as Knox Keesee threw for five touchdowns in leading the Vikings to a 42-13 Region 1–5A victory over the Trailblazers at the Stone Castle. It was final game in Jenkins' tutelage at Daniel Boone, which began in 2004. He played also played four years and served as an assistant for four seasons with the 'Blazers. "Our kids played hard. As far as me it has not been about me all year long," said Jenkins, who won 125 games at Daniel Boone, and four more in 2003 at Sullivan South. "I told them at the first of the year we have won several games on this field, we have had a lot of good players, a lot of good teams, a lot of good coaching staffs. "The thing that I am the most proud of is I have had 19 people work under me that are a head coach somewhere and I think that speaks a lot for what we have done." It was another special night in a special season for Tennessee High senior running back Elijah Plumbar, who ran for 203 yards and a first quarter touchdown, becoming the Vikings' all-time single season rushing leader, passing the 1,735 yards set by Todd Daggs in 1984. Plumbar set the single game mark of 327 yards in the previous game against Sevier County. "Plumbar is a special kid, there has not been many that has come through here like him and I don't think there ever will be," Tennessee High head coach Josh Holt said. "He is breaking all those records that have stood for a long time and there have been a lot of good running backs come through this place. He would be the first to tell you he can't do it without those guys up front and they really do a good job paving the way for him." With the Trailblazers focused on slowing down Plumbar, who had 165 yards in the opening half, the Vikings went to the air, led by Keesee, who completed seven passes for 123 yards, with five of them going for touchdowns. Cannon Swift caught scores from 39, 13 and 21 yards, while Bo Utsman hit pay dirt from nine and seven yards. Tennessee High scored on all four of its possessions in the first half to take a 28-0 lead into the halftime break. If David Crockett beats winless Cocke County on Friday, the Vikings (7-3, 3-2) will finish third in Region 1-5A and will face a playoff road game next Friday what is expected to be Knox Central. Meanwhile, Daniel Boone (2-8, 1-4), which won just six games over the last four seasons after finishing 12-1 in 2022, was led by Dru Fleming, who passed the 1,000 yard mark on the season with 136 of them, including a 1-yard touchdown run to narrow the margin to 35-7 going into the final period. The Trailblazers scored on the final play of Jenkins' career at Daniel Boone as a scrambling Mykah Lucas connected with Walker Barton on a 28-yard touchdown pass. Jenkins had one final meeting with his team, and reflected on a career that isn't over yet. Jenkins, who was quick to credit his wife, Lori, for being there for him over the years, expects to stay active in the game, perhaps as an assisant coach. "I am excited about this young group coming back. Our goal was to get this group to the playoffs, that was my goal, we fell short of that, but at the same time the good Lord knows what is best so we have just got to keep on plugging and keep on going," Jenkins said. "My best of luck for that group, whoever comes in and I will always be pulling for them and then we will go on. "I don't know what it will be like in the morning when I wake up because I am used to doing film in the mornings. It is just going to be different. We will see." Jenkins was already planning his football fix on Friday night in Kingsport. "I love football, I love watching young men grow," Jenkins said. "Who knows what the future holds. I could be back out somewhere so we will just see how it goes. I am going to enjoy this, I am going to watch D-B and Science Hill tomorrow night, eat some popcorn and be ready to go." *** Daniel Boone 0 0 7 0 — 7 Tennessee High 14 14 7 7 — 42 First Quarter TH—Elijah Plumbar 4 run (Joseph Farrell kick) 6:52 TH—Cannon Swift 39 pass from Knox Keesee (Farrell kick) 2:25 Second Quarter TH—Bo Utsman 9 pass from Keesee (Farrell kick) 7:13 TH—Swift 13 pass from Keesee (Farrell kick) 4:32 Third Quarter TH—Swift 21 pass from Keesse (Farrell kick) 10:49 DB—Dru Fleming 1 run (Judah Jackson kick) 1:08 Fourth Quarter TH—Utsman 7 pass from Keesee (Farrell kick) 7:33 DB—Walker Barton 28 pass from Mykah Lucas 0:00
